claims.text: A refractory high-entropy alloy can be used as an interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed interlayer is tungsten-based and contains deliberate Ta and Cr additions.
The HEA interlayer will provide a graded transition between the mechanical and thermal properties of W and CuCrZr.
The HEA composition can be tuned to have a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
The W-Ta-Cr-containing HEA will have robust diffusion-barrier properties at the joint interfaces.
W and CuCrZr have inherently different thermal expansion behavior.
W and CuCrZr have different interfacial diffusion behavior.
Matching the interlayer's thermal expansion behavior more closely to both adjoining materials will reduce interfacial stress concentrations.
The HEA interlayer will limit detrimental interdiffusion between W and CuCrZr.
Direct bonding of W and CuCrZr would promote the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
The HEA interlayer will mitigate the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
A W/HEA/CuCrZr joint will have lower residual stresses than a directly bonded W-CuCrZr joint.
A W/HEA/CuCrZr joint will exhibit less interfacial degradation than a directly bonded W-CuCrZr joint.
A W/HEA/CuCrZr joint will have improved mechanical stability under fusion-reactor conditions relative to a direct W-CuCrZr joint.
Direct W-CuCrZr joints are prone to problems caused by thermal-expansion mismatch under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Direct W-CuCrZr joints are prone to interfacial interdiffusion under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The interlayer's benefits may diminish outside its optimized temperature, irradiation, or thermal-cycling ranges.
Unexpected phase transformations in the HEA may diminish its effectiveness as an interlayer.
